_comment: Erzeugt aus docs/en und dem englischen Buch von `dhrt doku prosa` -- NICHT von Hand aendern. Der Hover nimmt sie mit DHRT_LANG=en.

docs.ALPHA: read the alpha channel (0..255) from a colour
docs.ANIM_FSM_FORCE: force a state (without conditions) — e.g. reset/respawn
docs.ANIM_FSM_LOAD: load + validate a .dhanim, starting in the default state
docs.ANIM_FSM_SETUP: register the frame ranges of all states as sprite animations + play the default
docs.ANIM_FSM_TRIGGER: fire a trigger (consumed by the next UPDATE)
docs.ANIM_FSM_UPDATE: advance the animation, evaluate transitions, play on a change. TRUE = state changed
docs.APPENDFILE: append text at the end (creates the file)
docs.ARC: arc segment in the bounding box; angles in radians, counter-clockwise. width (float, optional) = stroke width; without it 1px (independent of zoom), with it scaled with the CAMERA_SET zoom like LINEW/SPLINE
docs.ARG$: argument no. n (0-based); out of range → ""
docs.ARGC: number of arguments for this program
docs.ARRAY_AVG: average (the array must not be empty)
docs.ARRAY_FILL: fill all elements with wert (IN PLACE, every dimension)
docs.ARRAY_FILTER: new array with the elements for which funktion(x) returns TRUE (same element type)
docs.ARRAY_FIND: index of the first element for which funktion(x) returns TRUE, otherwise -1
docs.ARRAY_INSERT: insert at index idx (0..len); new length
docs.ARRAY_MAP: new array with funktion(x) for each element, e.g. ARRAY_MAP(a, FUNCTION(x) x * 2)
docs.ARRAY_POP: remove and return the last element (not empty)
docs.ARRAY_PUSH: append an element at the end; returns the new length
docs.ARRAY_REDUCE: folds the array: funktion(bisher, x) for each element, starting with start
docs.ARRAY_REMOVE_AT: remove and return the element at idx
docs.ASC: Code point of the first character. ASC("Anna") = 65.
docs.ASSERT: fails if the condition is FALSE
docs.ASSERT_EQ: the same, the message shows both values
docs.ASSERT_REPORT: print the summary, return the number of failures
docs.ASTAR_CLEAR_PATH: delete only the path data, walls stay
docs.ASTAR_FIND: BOOLEAN — TRUE if a path was found
docs.ASTAR_HEIGHT: INTEGER — size of the grid in tiles
docs.ASTAR_PATH_LEN: INTEGER — 0 if there is no path
docs.ASTAR_PATH_X: INTEGER — tile coordinate of the waypoint (0 = start)
docs.ASTAR_PATH_Y: INTEGER — tile coordinate of the waypoint (0 = start)
docs.ASTAR_WIDTH: INTEGER — size of the grid in tiles
docs.ATLAS_DRAW_FLIPPED: sub-sprite with mirroring (X/Y, each TRUE/FALSE or 1/0); optional tint
docs.ATLAS_LOAD: load an atlas from a JSON manifest
docs.AUDIO_AUTOPAN: endless swinging left↔right (starts left); tiefe 0..1 = deflection around the centre, periode_s <= 0 switches it off
docs.AUDIO_BUSY_CHANNELS: how many channels are playing right now
docs.AUDIO_BUS_PAN: Moves a whole bus in the stereo image (-1 = left, 0 = centre, +1 = right).
docs.AUDIO_CLOCK_NEW: AUDIO_CLOCK — create a clock — it starts paused
docs.AUDIO_CLOCK_PAUSE: pause; the tick counter stays where it is
docs.AUDIO_CLOCK_START: let it run (also again after PAUSE)
docs.AUDIO_CLOCK_STOP: stop and set the tick counter to 0
docs.AUDIO_CLOCK_TICKING: BOOLEAN — is it running right now?
docs.AUDIO_CLOCK_TICKS: INTEGER — how many ticks have passed?
docs.AUDIO_COMPRESSOR: dynamics compressor (glue/pump). threshold_db typ. −24..0, ratio ≥ 1 (1 = off), makeup_db level boost afterwards
docs.AUDIO_DELAY: echo. mix 0..1 (0 = off), feedback 0..0.95 (decay per repetition, default 0.5), time_ms echo time 1..4000 (changeable at run time, default 300; omitted = unchanged)
docs.AUDIO_DEPTH: INTEGER — how deep is the stack right now?
docs.AUDIO_DISTORTION: overdrive/fuzz. amount 0..1 (0 = off, → 0..36 dB drive), mix 0..1 (default 1.0)
docs.AUDIO_EMITTER_NEW: AUDIO_EMITTER sound source in space; at full volume up to min_dist, silent from max_dist
docs.AUDIO_EQ: parametric bell EQ (one band). gain_db 0 = transparent, >0 boost / <0 cut, q bandwidth (default 1)
docs.AUDIO_FFT: Fills a dimensioned ARRAY OF FLOAT with the band levels of the sound BEING HEARD AT THAT MOMENT.
docs.AUDIO_FILTER: low-pass. cutoff_hz 20..20000 (≤0 or ≥20000 = open/off), resonance 0..1 (emphasis at the cutoff — the “weeoow" SID/acid character)
docs.AUDIO_INIT: makes sure the audio system is running. Accepts arguments and ignores them -- they date from the mixer era and are only tolerated for compatibility
docs.AUDIO_IS_PLAYING: Is the channel playing right now?
docs.AUDIO_LFO_NEW: AUDIO_MOD — create an oscillating modulator (sine, triangle, saw, pulse)
docs.AUDIO_LFO_SET: change the oscillation while running; omitted values stay
docs.AUDIO_LISTENER_NEW: AUDIO_LISTENER place the ear; unrotated it looks along -Z
docs.AUDIO_LISTENER_SET_ORIENTATION: viewing direction around the Y axis, in degrees
docs.AUDIO_LISTENER_SET_POSITION: move the ear (e.g. following the camera)
docs.AUDIO_LOFI: Gives a freshly created sound (TONE/NOISE/SFX/SAMPLE) a grainy retro character: bit-crush (8 bit by default) plus a soft low-pass filter (3300 Hz by default) — the typical Amiga lo-fi sound.
docs.AUDIO_MODULATE: bind a modulator to a bus parameter; its range is mapped to min..max
docs.AUDIO_MOD_REMOVE: free the modulator — the parameter stays at its last value
docs.AUDIO_MUSIC_PAUSE: Pauses or resumes the music, stops it (optionally with a fade-out in milliseconds), and with POSITION gives the current playback time in seconds (FLOAT) — to synchronise a light show to the music, for instance.
docs.AUDIO_MUSIC_PITCH: music pitch (1.0 = normal; survives LOAD/QUEUE — slow-motion effect)
docs.AUDIO_MUSIC_PLAY: start (loops = -1 = endless = default; loops = N → N+1 passes)
docs.AUDIO_MUSIC_QUEUE: next track, as soon as the current one ends
docs.AUDIO_MUSIC_SEEK: jump to this point (seconds from the beginning)
docs.AUDIO_NOTE: a held note with a real ADSR envelope, vibrato, detune layer and portamento — the instrument for trackers and music
docs.AUDIO_PAN_POS: set the position directly (ends a running animation)
docs.AUDIO_PAN_SLIDE: one-time move from → to; stays at the target
docs.AUDIO_PITCH: pitch/speed: 1.0 = normal, 2.0 = an octave higher, 0.5 = lower
docs.AUDIO_PLAY_AT: Plans a sound's start exactly on the clock tick given — triggered by the audio thread itself, not by your frame timing.
docs.AUDIO_PLAY_ON: Plays a sound on an emitter rather than on the ordinary sfx bus — the panning and the volume by distance run automatically.
docs.AUDIO_POP: bring them back; without a previous PUSH this is an error
docs.AUDIO_PUSH: push all bus settings onto the stack
docs.AUDIO_REVERB: reverb. mix 0..1 (0 = off), feedback 0..1 (reverb length, default 0.9), damping 0..1 (treble damping, default 0.1)
docs.AUDIO_SAVE_WAV: save as a WAV file (bits = 16, the default, or 8)
docs.AUDIO_SET_NUM_CHANNELS: number of simultaneous channels (default 16, raise it for bullet hell)
docs.AUDIO_SOUND_COUNT: number of live (not freed) sound slots — diagnostics against sound leaks
docs.AUDIO_SOUND_MIX: add the source into the target from offset_ms
docs.AUDIO_SOUND_NEW: silence of the given length, as a canvas
docs.AUDIO_SOUND_NORMALIZE: bring the loudest point to spitze (default 1.0); returns the factor
docs.AUDIO_SOUND_WAVE: anzahl points of the waveform, -1..1 — for drawing
docs.AUDIO_STOP: stop the channel, optionally fade out
docs.AUDIO_TWEENER_NEW: AUDIO_MOD — modulator that moves to a target on command
docs.AUTOMATION_COUNT: events in the running recording or in the loaded file
docs.AUTOMATION_FRAME: frame number within the playback (0 = first)
docs.AUTOMATION_PLAY: load a recording and play it from the next frame on; returns the number of events loaded
docs.AUTOMATION_PLAYING: is a playback running? (becomes FALSE by itself after the last event)
docs.AUTOMATION_STOP: ends recording or playback; writes the recording to its file and returns the number of events
docs.BASE64_DECODE: Base64 to UTF-8 text (throws on invalid input)
docs.BATCH_DRAW: second name for ATLAS_DRAW — draws immediately, collects nothing
docs.BATCH_FLUSH: does nothing (no-op) — only so that old code keeps running
docs.BBOX_WIRES: box as edges between two corners (the order does not matter); with MODEL_BBOX the frame around a model
docs.BETWEEN$: what lies between the first links (from character ab, 0-based like MID$) and the next rechts; "" if one of them is missing
docs.BEZIER: quadratic Bézier curve from (x1, y1) to (x2, y2), bent towards the control point (kx, ky)
docs.BEZIER3: cubic Bézier curve with two control points (S-curves, connecting lines between nodes)
docs.BILLBOARD: image in space that always turns towards the camera (trees, sparks, labels)
docs.BILLBOARD_EX: with its own width and height, rotated around its centre (degrees) — spinning sparks, stretched beams
docs.BILLBOARD_PART: only a section of the image — a single frame from a sprite sheet, that is how characters walk in 3D; groesse is the height, the width follows the section
docs.BIN$: INTEGER as a binary/octal string (with sign)
docs.BLEND_MODE: blend mode for subsequent draws: "alpha" (default), "add" (additive – glow/light), "mult" (multiplicative – shadow/tint), "subtract"
docs.BOXROT: filled rectangle centred on (x, y), rotated about its centre (degrees, clockwise like DRAWIMAGEROT)
docs.BT_CHARACTERISTICS: STRING (multi-line uuid properties) which characteristics does a service have -- and what can be done with them?
docs.BT_CONNECT: BT_HANDLE — establish a connection to a device
docs.BT_IS_CONNECTED: BOOLEAN — is the connection still up?
docs.BT_READ: STRING (bytes as latin-1) read the value of a characteristic
docs.BT_SCAN: STRING (multi-line addr name rssi), 0..300s search for devices in range
docs.BT_SERVICES: STRING (multi-line UUIDs) which services does the device offer?
docs.BT_WRITE: write the value of a characteristic
docs.BUFFER_AUS_ZEIGER: copies laenge (length) bytes behind a pointer into a new BUFFER; 0 bytes give an empty one, a null pointer with a length is an error
docs.BUFFER_DEFLATE: compress bytes with Deflate ("zlib" default, "roh" = raw)
docs.BUFFER_RESIZE: grows with zeros, shrinks by cutting off
docs.BUFFER_ZEIGER: the address of the bytes of a BUFFER, for a struct field that points to another buffer; an empty buffer gives 0
docs.CAMEL$: identifier notations: "max hp", "MaxHp", "max_hp" or "max-hp" become maxHp, max_hp, MaxHp. Words are separated by whitespace, _, -, ., the change from lower to upper case and the end of an abbreviation (HTTPServer → http_server)
docs.CAMERA3D: set the camera: position, look-at target, field of view in degrees (usually 45). Up is +Y
docs.CAMERA3D_MOVE: move the camera from the program (in units, forward/right on the ground plane) and turn it (degrees: yaw to the right, pitch upwards, at most 89 degrees); zoom changes the distance to the target (positive = farther away). For your own key bindings, gamepad or camera flights; works from the position that CAMERA3D last set — so do not call CAMERA3D again in every frame
docs.CAMERA3D_PROJECTION: set your own projection matrix — for example parallel instead of perspective
docs.CAMERA3D_TARGET_X: FLOAT — what is it looking at?
docs.CAMERA3D_TARGET_Y: FLOAT — what is it looking at?
docs.CAMERA3D_TARGET_Z: FLOAT — what is it looking at?
docs.CAMERA3D_UPDATE: let raylib move the camera: 1 free, 2 orbital, 3 first person, 4 third person — reads mouse and WASD itself
docs.CAMERA3D_VIEW: set your own view matrix instead of the one built from CAMERA3D(...)
docs.CAMERA3D_X: FLOAT — where is the camera right now?
docs.CAMERA3D_Y: FLOAT — where is the camera right now?
docs.CAMERA3D_Z: FLOAT — where is the camera right now?
docs.CAMERA_FOLLOW: centres the camera on the target (rotation stays unchanged)
docs.CAMERA_ORBIT: Sets the 3D camera by spherical coordinates: it looks at the target (zx, zy, zz) and stands at distance radius, turned by gier (yaw, horizontal) and nick (pitch, vertical, in degrees).
docs.CAMERA_S2W_X: screen pixel to world coordinate (e.g. for a mouse click)
docs.CAMERA_S2W_Y: screen pixel to world coordinate (e.g. for a mouse click)
docs.CAMERA_SET: camera position (world point for the top left of the screen), zoom and optionally rotation
docs.CAMERA_SHAKE: screen shake: random camera jolting (world pixels), decays linearly over dauer_ms (default 300) — runs on its own, no per-frame code. staerke = 0 stops immediately
docs.CAPSULE: capsule between two points (cylinder with hemispheres) — the usual shape for characters and their collision
docs.CENT: INTEGER — convert an amount into whole cents — rounds instead of truncating; also accepts written amounts ("19,99", "1.234,56")
docs.CHART_CLICKED: point clicked in this frame, otherwise -1
docs.CHART_DATA: replace all values of a series (ARRAY OF FLOAT)
docs.CHART_NEW: Creates a chart and gives a CHART handle.
docs.CHART_PALETTE: A colour sequence of your own for the data series or pie slices (ARRAY OF INTEGER or TUPLE).
docs.CHART_PUSH: append a value at the end (live curves, see fenster)
docs.CHART_SET: Everything that is text: titel, einheit, achse_x, achse_y, legende (aus/oben/unten/links/rechts), ausrichtung (senkrecht/waagerecht), werte (aus/innen/aussen), wertanzeige (aus/innen/pille/blase/am_zeiger), zifferblatt (ring/segmente/striche/baender), punktform (kreis/quadrat/raute/dreieck).
docs.CHART_SET_COLOR: Everything that is a colour: hintergrund, rahmen, gitter, text, titel, achse, zeiger, flaeche, verlauf, schatten — and the directed scale gradient skala_von / skala_mitte / skala_bis.
docs.CHART_SET_FLAG: Everything that is a switch: rahmen, gitter_x, gitter_y, prozent, flaeche, punkte, glatt, null_linie, stapel, verlauf, treppe, fadenkreuz, hover, tooltip.
docs.CHART_SET_NUM: Everything that is a number: min, max, innenradius, ecken, polster, gitter (the SPACING of the grid lines, not how many), nachkomma, striche, unterstriche, linien_dicke, animation, fenster, schatten, deckkraft …
docs.CHART_THEME: Sets background, text, grid and data colours in one sweep: “dunkel”, “hell”, “neon” or “pastell”.
docs.CHART_VALUE: short form for series 0, point 0 — the gauge way
docs.CHART_ZONE: colour zones of the gauge scale, optionally labelled
docs.CHART_ZONE_CLEAR: colour zones of the gauge scale, optionally labelled
docs.CHAR_FACING: INTEGER (-1 = left, +1 = right) facing direction -- for mirroring the sprite
docs.CHAR_H: FLOAT — size of the collision box
docs.CHAR_NEW: CHAR_CONTROLLER create a controller -- (x,y) top-left corner, (w,h) size in pixels
docs.CHAR_ON_GROUND: BOOLEAN — is the character standing on solid ground?
docs.CHAR_ON_WALL_LEFT: BOOLEAN — is it touching a wall on the left or right?
docs.CHAR_ON_WALL_RIGHT: BOOLEAN — is it touching a wall on the left or right?
docs.CHAR_SET_COYOTE_TIME: 6 — for this many frames after leaving the edge a jump still counts
docs.CHAR_SET_JUMP_BUFFER: 6 — pressed this many frames before landing, the jump already counts
docs.CHAR_SET_MAX_FALL: 7.0 — maximum falling speed -- without it a character falls through thin floors
docs.CHAR_SET_VARIABLE_JUMP: TRUE — shorter jump on a short key press
docs.CHAR_SET_VARIABLE_JUMP_CUT: 0.5 (= Mario) the fraction the rising speed drops to on release
docs.CHAR_UPDATE: run one frame: compute velocity, collide, update position
docs.CHAR_W: FLOAT — size of the collision box
docs.CHR$: Unicode code point to a 1-character string. CHR$(65) = "A".
docs.CIRCLE3D: circle outline lying flat on the ground — target marker, range, shadow edge
docs.CIRCLEOUTLINE: circle as outline only (counterpart to CIRCLE)
docs.CIRCLE_GRADIENT: circle with a gradient from the centre (innen) to the edge (aussen); with RGBA as the edge colour, a soft glow
docs.CLIPBOARD_GET: read text from the clipboard; empty if another program is holding it right now
docs.CLIPBOARD_SET: put text into the clipboard — an error if that does not succeed
docs.CLOUD_CONFIGURE: set the server address + shared secret (once)
docs.CLOUD_LAST_ERROR$: empty after success; otherwise the last error message (network/auth/server)
docs.CLOUD_LOAD: loads the stored string — empty if nothing has been saved yet OR on an error
docs.CLOUD_SAVE: stores data$ in full (overwrites a previous state)
docs.CLS: fill the buffer with color (default: black)
docs.CODE_CHECK$: STRING (JSON) the front-end chain like dhrt --check: a list of {zeile, spalte, laenge, schwere, meldung} with schwere = fehler/warnung; spalte (from 1) and laenge say where in the line the message belongs -- the location of a syntax error, otherwise a name mentioned in the message, otherwise the line without indentation; basis$ = folder for IMPORT "x.dh" (default: the working directory). Lines …
docs.CODE_COMPLETE: ARRAY OF STRING suggestions for the word beginning to the left of the position: own symbols, commands, keywords, constants
docs.CODE_DEFINITION: TUPLE (zeile, spalte) where the word is defined; (-1, -1) if there is no definition in this text
docs.CODE_FORMAT$: STRING — the source formatted as by dhrt fmt: keywords in upper case, trailing whitespace removed, with einruecken (default TRUE) the blocks re-indented; empty if the source cannot be read (syntax error)
docs.CODE_HOVER$: STRING — signature and description of the word at that position as Markdown; empty if there is no word there
docs.CODE_NAMES: MAP OF INTEGER how often each name is used (lower case, including $): without comments and strings and without the place where a SUB/FUNCTION defines it -- calls, FUNCREFs and methods after a dot count
docs.CODE_REFERENCES: ARRAY OF INTEGER the lines of all occurrences
docs.CODE_RENAME$: STRING — the source with the name at this position renamed to neu$ everywhere — whole words, without comments and strings. Empty if there is no name there, it is a keyword or neu$ is not a name
docs.CODE_SYMBOLS$: STRING (JSON) the outline: {name, art, von, bis, kinder} — classes with their methods; art is class, struct, sub, function, property or enum
docs.CODE_TYPES$: STRING (JSON) type hints for an editor: for each place without a written type -- today the variables of FOR EACH -- {"zeile", "name", "typ"} (line from 1; MAP yields keys as STRING, in the pair form plus the value); what the compiler does not know is left out
docs.COLLIDES: AABB collision of two rectangles. Touching does not count (equal edges → FALSE).
docs.COLOR_LERP: mix two colours channel by channel (t 0..1)
docs.COMPRESS$: STRING — pack text (DEFLATE); the result is Base64, because strings are UTF-8 here and raw compressor output would not be
docs.CONTAINS: substring contained? (function form of teil IN s)
docs.CORO_DONE: BOOLEAN — whether the coroutine has finished.
docs.CORO_RESULT: Final RETURN value (throws if not finished yet).
docs.CORO_RESUME: Continue up to the next YIELD; returns the YIELD value (or the RETURN value when the coroutine ends).
docs.CORO_SEND: Like CORO_RESUME, but the YIELD expression in the body evaluates to v.
docs.COUNT: number of non-overlapping occurrences of teil
docs.CRC32: CRC-32 checksum of the UTF-8 bytes
docs.CSV_ROW$: a single row from a 1D array
docs.CURRENT_MONITOR: index of the monitor the window mostly lies on right now
docs.CURVE_BSPLINE: FLOAT — cubic B-spline: passes smoothly by the points instead of through them (like SPLINE_BASIS)
docs.CURVE_LERP: FLOAT — linear interpolation a + (b - a) * t
docs.CYLINDER: cylinder — with r_oben = 0 it becomes a cone
docs.CYLINDER_EX: cylinder (or cone) from one point to another, in any direction — pipes, branches, beams
docs.DB_BEGIN: begin, commit, roll back a transaction
docs.DB_CLOSE_RESULT: release a result if you do not read it to the end
docs.DB_COL_COUNT: INTEGER — number of columns in the result
docs.DB_COL_NAME: STRING — name of the column (index from 0)
docs.DB_COMMIT: begin, commit, roll back a transaction
docs.DB_EXEC: INTEGER (rowcount) SQL without a result set (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/CREATE); bind values with ?, returns the number of affected rows
docs.DB_GET_BOOL: BOOLEAN — read a column of the current row as a truth value (0/1 in SQLite)
docs.DB_GET_FLOAT: FLOAT — read a column of the current row as a floating-point number
docs.DB_GET_INT: INTEGER — read a column of the current row as an integer
docs.DB_GET_STRING: STRING — read a column of the current row as text (index from 0)
docs.DB_KIND$: STRING — which database: sqlite, postgres or mysql
docs.DB_LAST_ROWID: INTEGER — ID of the most recently inserted row (SQLite rowid, MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT, PostgreSQL lastval())
docs.DB_NEXT: BOOLEAN — advance by one row; FALSE when there are no more
docs.DB_OPEN: DB_CONN — open a database: a file (created if it does not exist; ":memory:" = volatile), postgres://... or mysql://...
docs.DB_PING: BOOLEAN — is the connection still up? (a file always is; a server answers within 5 s or not)
docs.DB_QUERY: DB_RESULT — run a SELECT and return a cursor on the result
docs.DB_QUERY_PENDING: how many queries are still open
docs.DB_QUERY_READY: is the result there? (checks, does not wait)
docs.DB_QUERY_RESULT: fetch the result and free the slot
docs.DB_QUERY_START: starts in the background, immediately returns the job number (a file or a server, as with DB_OPEN)
docs.DB_ROLLBACK: begin, commit, roll back a transaction
docs.DELTA: Gives the time elapsed since the last FLIP, in seconds (a small decimal).
docs.DIRLIST_REC: as above, but recursive — files only, relative paths with /
docs.DRAWFPS: show the frame rate as “60 FPS” in the built-in font, in screen coordinates (the camera does not apply); without a colour green, below 30 orange, below 15 red
docs.DRAWIMAGE9: 9-slice: the image stretched into the rectangle, the four corners at their own size, the edges in one direction only, the centre in both — for frames, panels and buttons that grow to any size without distorting. Edges in pixels of the image; if the target does not fit, the corners shrink proportionally. Camera-aware.
docs.DRAWIMAGEPART: draw a sub-rectangle from a sheet
docs.DRAWIMAGEPARTEX: Like DRAWIMAGEPART, but with a target size of your own (w, h) rather than 1:1 — the section is stretched or squeezed to the target size as it is drawn.
docs.DRAWIMAGEROT: centred on (x,y), rotated by winkel degrees (about the centre), optionally scaled + tinted. Ideal for rotated sprites / physics2d (winkel = DEG(PHYS2D_BODY_ANGLE(...))). Camera-aware.
docs.DRAWTILEMAP: Draws a two-dimensional array of tile numbers as a map.
docs.ECS_ADD_INT: Hangs a named value on an entity.
docs.ECS_COUNT_WITH: O(1) — number of holders of a component
docs.ECS_DESTROY: BOOLEAN — TRUE if removed, FALSE if it did not exist
docs.ECS_INTEGRATE_FLOAT: target += delta for all entities with both components
docs.ECS_QUERY2: ARRAY OF INTEGER — entities with n1 AND n2
docs.ECS_QUERY3: ARRAY OF INTEGER — entities with n1 AND n2 AND n3
docs.ELLIPSE: filled ellipse, fitted into the bounding box
docs.ENUM_NAME: return the name for an ENUM value — for display and debugging
docs.EOF: TRUE when there is nothing more to read from the file: WHILE NOT EOF(f) : PRINT READLINE(f) : WEND
docs.EPRINT: line to stderr instead of stdout
docs.EURO$: STRING — display a cent amount in German notation (1999 becomes 19,99 €)
docs.EXEPATH$: path of the running program file
docs.EXIT: end immediately, code = return value (0..255, default 0)
docs.FBM: several noise layers stacked: coarse shape plus fine detail
docs.FILES_DROPPED: how many files were dragged into the window in this frame or (macOS) handed over by the Finder? Holds for exactly one frame, can be queried any number of times
docs.FILETIME: last modified, seconds as in the module zeit
docs.FILE_DROPPED: path of the i-th of them
docs.FILE_SAVE_DIALOG: choose a file to save (default$ = suggested file name)
docs.FIRMATA_ANALOG_READ: INTEGER (0..16383) read an analogue value -- careful, what counts here is the channel (A0 = 0), not the pin number
docs.FIRMATA_ANALOG_WRITE: output a PWM value (0..255), e.g. for brightness or motor speed
docs.FIRMATA_DIGITAL_READ: BOOLEAN — read the reported state of an input -- the value comes from the last FIRMATA_UPDATE
docs.FIRMATA_DIGITAL_WRITE: switch a pin HIGH or LOW
docs.FIRMATA_IS_OPEN: BOOLEAN — is the connection still up?
docs.FIRMATA_OPEN: FIRMATA_HANDLE establish the connection to the board (StandardFirmata must be running there)
docs.FIRMATA_PIN_MODE: set the operating mode of a pin (input, output, PWM, analogue)
docs.FIRMATA_PORTS: STRING (comma-separated list of available ports, like SERIAL_PORTS()) which serial ports are there?
docs.FIRMATA_UPDATE: call once per frame: fetches the pin states reported by the board
docs.FLIP: output the frame to the screen (synchronized to 60 FPS)
docs.FLT: Turns a whole number (or a decimal) into a decimal (FLOAT) — the counterpart to INT.
docs.FONT_GLYPH_WIDTH: how far TEXT advances after this character at groesse points — measured like TEXT_WIDTH, without switching the active font
docs.FONT_HAS_GLYPH: does the font itself have a glyph for it? If not, TEXT draws it with the fallback font; -1 = built-in font
docs.FONT_HAS_STYLE: TRUE if this face exists as a file -- otherwise the runtime imitates it
docs.FONT_STYLE: the real bold/italic face of a loaded font (looks for the file next to it, e.g. segoeuib.ttf for segoeui.ttf); if there is none, font itself comes back
docs.FONT_TO_IMAGE: the characters erstes..letztes (default 32..126, at most 256) as an image in the format of LOADFONT_IMAGE: each character white in a transparent field, magenta (&HFF00FF) outside and in between. That turns a vector font into a pixel font that you can touch up and load again with LOADFONT_IMAGE(bild, &HFF00FF, erstes)
docs.FORMAT$: printf style. FORMAT$(42, "%05d") → "00042". Six specifiers: %d/%i, %f, %x, %X, %s — plus %% for a literal percent sign. Width, zeros and precision as usual (%05d, %-6d, %.2f). Anything else reports "unknown specifier"
docs.GELD_CENT: to whole cents, rounded commercially (half up)
docs.GELD_TEILEN: split up without losing a cent

docs.GUI_TEXTAREA_ABBREV_HIT: which abbreviation Tab hit in this frame (-1 = none); applies for one frame like GUI_CLICKED

docs.GUI_TEXTAREA_CURSOR: where the cursor is (from 1, in characters)

docs.GUI_TEXTAREA_SELECT: select a range, cursor at the end

docs.SHADOW_AREA: which section gets shadows — small = sharp, large = covers more
docs.SHADOW_ENABLE: switch shadow casting on; the first directional light casts it
docs.SHADOW_TARGET: what that section is centred on (usually the player character)
docs.SHELL: start a program, wait, return value
docs.SHELL_CODE: return value of the most recently fetched task
docs.SHELL_OUT$: like SHELL, but collects the output
docs.SHELL_START: starts in the background, returns the task number
docs.SIZEOF: size of a STRUCT … LAYOUT C or of a type word in bytes, computed at compile time
docs.SKYBOX: also show the panorama as the background (needs LIGHT_ENV_HDR)
docs.SKYBOX_IMAGE: sky from an ordinary image instead of a .hdr file: six faces as a strip (6:1 or 1:6) or as a cross (4:3 or 3:4), order +X, −X, +Y, −Y, +Z, −Z; shows it right away, SKYBOX(FALSE) hides it
docs.SLEEP: waits ms milliseconds without freezing the window
docs.SMTP_ATTACH: attach a file — can be called several times
docs.SMTP_TO: recipient — can be called several times
docs.SNAKE$: identifier notations: "max hp", "MaxHp", "max_hp" or "max-hp" become maxHp, max_hp, MaxHp. Words are separated by whitespace, _, -, ., the change from lower to upper case and the end of an abbreviation (HTTPServer → http_server)
docs.SORT: sort / reverse a 1D array IN PLACE
docs.SPEAK: speaks text$; unterbrechen (interrupt) = abort the running announcement and speak immediately, otherwise append at the end
docs.SPEAKING: BOOLEAN — is an announcement still running or waiting?
docs.SPEAK_SOUND: SOUND — synthesize only — a sound as from AUDIO_NOTE, for AUDIO_PLAY, AUDIO_PLAY_ON(emitter), AUDIO_SOUND_MIX, AUDIO_SAVE_WAV
docs.SPEAK_VOICE: choose a voice (a name from SPEAK_VOICES(), case does not matter); empty = system voice. Unknown = error
docs.SPEAK_VOICES: ARRAY OF STRING the installed voices, e.g. Katja, Stefan, Hedda
docs.SPEAK_WAIT: blocks until everything has been spoken (for console programs before INPUT; in a game better ask SPEAKING())
docs.SPLINE: smooth Catmull-Rom curve through the points; xs/ys are ARRAY OF INTEGER of equal length
docs.SPLINE_BASIS: B-spline: even smoother than SPLINE, but does not run through the points, it is pulled by them (at least 4)
docs.SPLINE_BEZIER: chain of cubic Bézier curves: start, then two control points and one end each (4, 7, 10 … points) — the way drawing programs store paths
docs.SPLIT$: Splits s$ at the separator into an ARRAY OF STRING.
docs.SPRITE_COLLIDE: do two sprites overlap? (rectangle against rectangle)
docs.SPRITE_HIT_BOX: AABB test of the sprite against a rectangle (x, y, w, h)
docs.SPRITE_HIT_POINT: is the point (x, y) inside the sprite? (mouse click test)
docs.SPRITE_IS_FINISHED: has a PLAY_ONCE animation reached the end?
docs.STDIN: standard input as a file handle
docs.STOPMUSIC: one stream at a time. Refilling happens on the audio thread, not in the game loop: there is no update_stream call per FLIP (exactly the point where raylib audio crackled). Music loops endlessly — play_music passes on loops = -1, which becomes a loop_region(0.0..) in Kira.
docs.STR$: Value to string. Bools become "TRUE"/"FALSE", floats like 3.0 become "3.0".
docs.TASK_PENDING: tasks that have not been fetched yet
docs.TEMPFILE$: a free name in the temp directory, created empty
docs.TEXTROT: text centred on (x, y), rotated about the centre (degrees, like DRAWIMAGEROT) and scaled — for score pop-ups, slanted labels. Uses the active font/size
docs.TEXT_AUS_ZEIGER$: copies the text behind a pointer up to the null character (UTF-8; with breit (wide) = TRUE wchar_t, i.e. UTF-16 on Windows); 0 gives ""
docs.TEXT_BOLD: switch only bold or italic on or off; the rest of the style stays
docs.TEXT_GET_STYLE$: the current style as text, e.g. "fett+kursiv"
docs.TEXT_HEIGHT: line height of the active font
docs.TEXT_ITALIC: switch only bold or italic on or off; the rest of the style stays
docs.TEXT_SIZE: font size for subsequent TEXT calls (4–400)
docs.TEXT_STYLE: style for subsequent TEXT calls: fett (bold), kursiv (italic), unterstrichen (underlined), durchgestrichen (strikethrough), joined with + ("fett+unterstrichen"); "normal" switches back
docs.TEXT_WIDTH: pixel width of s$ in the active font/size
docs.TILED_ADD_LAYER: INTEGER (index) append an empty tile layer
docs.TILED_ADD_OBJECT: INTEGER (index) put an object into an object layer
docs.TILED_ADD_TILESET: INTEGER (index) append a tileset; the runtime assigns the firstgid itself
docs.TILED_COUNT_GID: INTEGER — how often does this GID occur in the layer?
docs.TILED_FILL_RECT: INTEGER — fill a rectangle with a GID; returns the number of changed tiles
docs.TILED_FLOOD_FILL: INTEGER — paint bucket: recolour the connected area starting at (tx,ty)
docs.TILED_LAYER_COUNT: INTEGER — how many layers does the map have?
docs.TILED_LAYER_HEIGHT: INTEGER (tile layers only) size of the layer in tiles
docs.TILED_LAYER_INDEX: INTEGER (-1 if not present) find a layer by its name
docs.TILED_LAYER_NAME: STRING — name of the layer (index from 0)
docs.TILED_LAYER_WIDTH: INTEGER (tile layers only) size of the layer in tiles
docs.TILED_MOVE_LAYER: move a layer to another position
docs.TILED_NEW: TILED_MAP — create an empty map -- without a layer and without a tileset
docs.TILED_OBJECT_COUNT: INTEGER — how many objects does this object layer have?
docs.TILED_OBJECT_HEIGHT: FLOAT — size of the object in pixels
docs.TILED_OBJECT_NAME: STRING — name of the object (index from 0)
docs.TILED_OBJECT_PROP_KEYS: ARRAY OF STRING the same for an object
docs.TILED_OBJECT_REMOVE_PROP: remove a property of an object
docs.TILED_OBJECT_SET_PROP: set a property of an object
docs.TILED_OBJECT_TYPE: STRING (Tiled "type" or "class") type of the object, as entered in Tiled
docs.TILED_OBJECT_WIDTH: FLOAT — size of the object in pixels
docs.TILED_OBJECT_X: FLOAT — position of the object in pixels
docs.TILED_OBJECT_Y: FLOAT — position of the object in pixels
docs.TILED_REPLACE: INTEGER — replace every GID from_gid with to_gid — swap a tileset without a loop
docs.TILED_SAVE: write the map as Tiled JSON
docs.TILED_TILESET_COUNT: INTEGER — how many tilesets does the map bring along?
docs.TILED_TILESET_FIRSTGID: INTEGER — first GID of this tileset -- this is how you map a GID to its tileset
docs.TILED_TILESET_IMAGE: STRING (absolute path to the tileset image) image file of the tileset
docs.TILED_TILESET_TILES: INTEGER — how many tiles does this tileset have?
docs.TILED_TILE_AT: INTEGER (GID, 0 = empty; OOB = 0) which tile is at this position?
docs.TILED_TILE_PROP_BOOL: BOOLEAN (FALSE if not set) read a property of the tile -- maintained per tile in Tiled (solid, damage, ...)
docs.TILED_TILE_PROP_FLOAT: FLOAT — property of the tile as a floating-point number
docs.TILED_TILE_PROP_INT: INTEGER (0 if not set) property of the tile as an integer
docs.TILED_TILE_PROP_KEYS: ARRAY OF STRING which properties does this tile have?
docs.TILED_TILE_PROP_STRING: STRING — property of the tile as text
docs.TILED_TILE_REMOVE_PROP: remove a property of a tile
docs.TILED_TILE_SET: INTEGER (old GID). 0 = delete the tile. OOB = no-op. set a tile
docs.TILED_TILE_SET_PROP: set a property of a tile
docs.TIMER_AFTER: call the FUNCREF once after ms; returns a timer ID
docs.TIMER_CLEAR: discard all timers + cooldowns (e.g. on a scene change)
docs.TIMER_EVERY: call the FUNCREF every ms (ms > 0); returns a timer ID
docs.TIMER_UPDATE: call once per frame -- fires the callbacks that are due
docs.TITLE$: first letter of each word upper case, the rest lower case
docs.TOUCH_ID: identifier of this finger — stays the same across frames as long as it stays down
docs.TRAY_CLICKED: was the icon clicked in this frame? Holds for exactly one frame, like GUI_CLICKED; Linux does not report a double click
docs.TRAY_DOUBLE_CLICKED: was the icon clicked in this frame? Holds for exactly one frame, like GUI_CLICKED; Linux does not report a double click
docs.TRAY_HIDE: remove the icon; is it showing right now? It disappears by itself when the program ends
docs.TRAY_MENU: the right-click menu (on macOS also Ctrl+click); the entries stand in one text separated by vertical bars, a single - is a separator, at most 64 entries
docs.TRAY_MENU_CLICKED$: the text of the menu entry chosen in this frame, otherwise ""
docs.TRAY_SHOW: show an icon in the notification area — on Windows in the taskbar, on macOS in the menu bar, on Linux in the desktop's panel (via D-Bus); without an image the one from WINDOW_ICON, otherwise the default icon; the hint appears on hover (default: the window title)
docs.TRAY_SHOWN: remove the icon; is it showing right now? It disappears by itself when the program ends
docs.TRAY_TOOLTIP: change the hint (to show progress, say)
docs.TRIANGLE3D: free triangle in space, visible from both sides
docs.TRYVAL: robust VAL: on a parse error default instead of a silent 0
docs.TWEEN_DONE: BOOLEAN (always FALSE for loop/pingpong) has it finished?
docs.TWEEN_EASINGS: STRING (comma-separated list) which easing curves are there?
docs.TWEEN_NEW_LOOP: TWEEN (forever, jumps back) like TWEEN_NEW, jumps back to the start at the end
docs.TWEEN_NEW_PINGPONG: TWEEN (forever, back & forth) like TWEEN_NEW, runs backwards at the end
docs.TWEEN_PAUSE: stop and let it run again
docs.TWEEN_PROGRESS: FLOAT (0.0 .. 1.0) how far along is it? (0 = start, 1 = end)
docs.TWEEN_RESUME: stop and let it run again
docs.TWEEN_VALUE: FLOAT — current value -- what you draw
docs.TYPEOF: runtime type name, e.g. "INTEGER", "STRING", "VEC3", "MAT4". For an instance the class name in upper case ("HUND")
docs.UI_BUTTON: BOOLEAN — TRUE if clicked in this frame
docs.UI_END_FRAME: mandatory at the end of every frame before FLIP()
docs.UI_RESET: clear all UI state + reset theme/metrics
docs.UI_TABLE: INTEGER — index of the clicked row (-1 if none)
docs.UI_TABLE_HEADER_CLICK: INTEGER — header column clicked in this frame (-1) — sorting hook
docs.UI_TABLE_SELECTED: INTEGER — persistently selected row (-1 if none)
docs.UI_THEME_GET: — / INT — set/read a single theme colour
docs.UI_THEME_SET: — / INT — set/read a single theme colour
docs.UI_WINDOW_BEGIN: BOOLEAN — movable window; FALSE if collapsed
docs.UNLOADSOUND: stop the sound and free its buffer — against buffers piling up with many AUDIO_TONE/AUDIO_SFX/AUDIO_NOISE notes (a long song). The handle stays valid; playing it again raises an error
docs.URL_DECODE: STRING — the counterpart — turn encoded text back
docs.URL_ENCODE: STRING — make text safe for a URL (spaces, umlauts, &)
docs.USB_LIST: STRING (multi-line vid:pid product manufacturer) list connected HID devices
docs.USB_MANUFACTURER: STRING — manufacturer name according to the device
docs.USB_OPEN: USB_HANDLE — open a device via vendor and product ID
docs.USB_OPEN_PATH: USB_HANDLE — open a device via its system path (unambiguous when two identical ones are plugged in)
docs.USB_PRODUCT: STRING — product name according to the device
docs.USB_READ: STRING (bytes as latin-1) read up to n bytes; after timeout_ms whatever is there is returned
docs.USB_SERIAL: STRING — serial number according to the device
docs.USB_WRITE: INTEGER (bytes written) send a report to the device
docs.VAL: The number at the start of the text (VAL("3 Äpfel") = 3), also &HFF/&O17/&B101/0x1F/0b11. With . or an exponent → FLOAT, otherwise INT. No number at the start → 0.
docs.VEC2_ANGLE: FLOAT — angle in radians (from the +x axis)
docs.VEC2_NORMALIZE: VEC2 — unit vector (NIL for a zero vector)
docs.VEC2_REFLECT: VEC2 — reflection off a wall normal
docs.VEC3_CROSS: VEC3 — cross product — perpendicular to both, for example for surface normals
docs.VEC3_DOT: FLOAT — dot product — 0 at a right angle, positive for the same direction
docs.VEC3_LENGTH_SQ: FLOAT — squared length — saves the square root when you only compare lengths
docs.VEC3_LERP: VEC3 — interpolate linearly between the two (t 0..1)
docs.VEC3_NORMALIZE: VEC3 — bring to length 1 (keeping the direction)
docs.VEC3_REFLECT: VEC3 — reflect off a surface with normal n — bouncing
docs.VEC3_TRANSFORM: VEC3 — send through the matrix as a point (w=1, translation applies)
docs.VEC3_TRANSFORM_DIR: VEC3 — as a direction (w=0, translation is ignored)
docs.VEC4_DOT: FLOAT — dot product over all four components
docs.VEC4_FROM_VEC3: VEC4 — extend a VEC3 by a fourth component (w=1 point, w=0 direction)
docs.VERSION$: the version of the runtime that is currently running (the same number as dhrt --version)
docs.VIDEO_DONE: has it (without looping) reached the end?
docs.VIDEO_DRAW: advance and draw the current frame
docs.VIDEO_FRAME: number of the frame currently in the IMAGE (from 0)
docs.VIDEO_FREE: free the video and its image
docs.VIDEO_IMAGE: the IMAGE that every new frame is written into
docs.VIDEO_LOAD: open an MP4 file, returns a VIDEO; the first frame is in the image right away
docs.VIDEO_LOOP: start over at the end instead of stopping
docs.VIDEO_PAUSE: pause, the frame stays where it is
docs.VIDEO_PLAY: play; a video that has run to the end starts over
docs.VIDEO_SEEK: jump to a position (clamped to the duration)
docs.VIDEO_STOP: stop and go back to the start
docs.VIDEO_UPDATE: advance the video's clock by DELTA() without drawing
docs.WAITKEY: stops until a key arrives and returns its code (-1 if the window is closed)
docs.WEIGHTED_CHOICE: element from werte, chosen in proportion to gewichte (1D arrays of equal length, weights ≥ 0). Loot tables.
docs.WIFI_AVAILABLE: BOOLEAN (true if Windows + Wi-Fi adapter) can the module be used here at all?
docs.WIFI_CONNECT: BOOLEAN (create profile + issue connect command) connect to a network -- creates a Windows profile in the process
docs.WIFI_CURRENT: STRING (current SSID, "" if not connected) which network is the computer connected to?
docs.WIFI_PROFILES: STRING (multi-line list of saved profiles) which networks are saved?
docs.WIFI_SCAN: STRING (multi-line ssid\ signal_pct, sorted by signal) search for reachable networks
docs.WIFI_SIGNAL: INTEGER (0..100, -1 if not connected) signal strength of the current connection
docs.WINDOW_CLOSE_REQUESTED: TRUE when the USER wants to close the window (the X, Alt+F4, the quit key) -- without the frame limit. The window stays open: a program with unsaved work asks first and then ends itself. An event, not a state -- it holds for one frame
docs.WINDOW_DPI_X: screen scaling (1.0 normal, 2.0 HiDPI) — without it a program cannot know whether its pixel sizes come out tiny on the target device
docs.WINDOW_DPI_Y: screen scaling (1.0 normal, 2.0 HiDPI) — without it a program cannot know whether its pixel sizes come out tiny on the target device
docs.WINDOW_ESC_QUIT: ESC as the window close key on/off (raylib default: on, with gui off from the first GUI_UPDATE on). With FALSE, ESC is a completely normal key (QUITREQUESTED is then only triggered by window X / Alt+F4) — for games that use ESC for the pause/main menu. An explicit WINDOW_ESC_QUIT(TRUE) applies with gui too
docs.WINDOW_FOCUS: bring your own window to the front
docs.WINDOW_FOCUSED: is the window in the foreground? — use it to pause when the user clicks away
docs.WINDOW_HIDE: make the window disappear, from the taskbar too, and bring it back — for tools that live in the tray
docs.WINDOW_ICON: Sets the window icon from an image loaded with LOADIMAGE.
docs.WINDOW_IS_FULLSCREEN: is it running in fullscreen right now?
docs.WINDOW_MAXIMIZE: bring the window to screen size
docs.WINDOW_MINIMIZE: put the window into the taskbar
docs.WINDOW_OPACITY: Makes the whole window translucent (1.0 = opaque, 0.0 = invisible) — for overlays, fade-ins, or a gentle appearance at startup.
docs.WINDOW_OPEN: start a second dhrt run datei$; numbers, texts, BOOLEAN become command-line arguments (ARGC/ARG$)
docs.WINDOW_PASSTHROUGH: pass mouse clicks through to the desktop (click-through widget)
docs.WINDOW_RECV$: next line from the child or ""
docs.WINDOW_RENDER_HEIGHT: the window's real pixel size — larger than SCREENWIDTH()/SCREENHEIGHT() on a HiDPI screen
docs.WINDOW_RENDER_WIDTH: the window's real pixel size — larger than SCREENWIDTH()/SCREENHEIGHT() on a HiDPI screen
docs.WINDOW_RESIZABLE: may the user drag the window's size? (default: no)
docs.WINDOW_RESIZED: TRUE in the frame in which the user changed the size — the right moment to recompute a layout, rather than doing so every frame.
docs.WINDOW_RESTORE: bring it back from maximized or minimized
docs.WINDOW_SEND: send one line — anything sent before the connection is delivered as soon as the child calls PARENT_*
docs.WINDOW_SHOW: make the window disappear, from the taskbar too, and bring it back — for tools that live in the tray
docs.WINDOW_TOPMOST: keep the window always in the foreground
docs.WINDOW_WAIT_EVENTS: FLIP waits for input, at most this long — a tool that only reacts to clicks then needs hardly any CPU time; 0 switches it off
docs.WINDOW_X: position of the window's top left corner (px)
docs.WINDOW_Y: position of the window's top left corner (px)
docs.WORLD_TO_SCREEN_X: FLOAT — where does a point of the world land on the screen? — for labels above characters
docs.WORLD_TO_SCREEN_Y: FLOAT — where does a point of the world land on the screen? — for labels above characters
docs.WRAP: fold v cyclically into [lo, hi) (angle/index wrap-around)
docs.XLSX_NEW: new workbook (first sheet is called Tabelle1)
docs.XLSX_SHEET: another sheet — and it becomes the active one
docs.XML_COUNT: how many with the same name?
docs.XML_TEXT$: the text (including that of the children)
docs.ZEIT_AUS_TEILEN: point in time from individual values
docs.ZEIT_DIFF: distance in seconds (negative if zeit is earlier)
docs.ZEIT_FORMAT$: point in time according to a pattern
docs.ZEIT_JETZT: now, as a point in time
docs.ZEIT_LESBAR: could the text be read? (asks, does not abort)
docs.ZEIT_PARSE: text to point in time; aborts on anything unreadable
docs.ZEIT_TEIL: one field: jahr, monat, tag, stunde, minute, sekunde (year, month, day, hour, minute, second)
docs.ZEIT_TEXT$: point in time as JJJJ-MM-TT hh:mm:ss (YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm:ss)
docs.ZIP_CREATE: archive from a list of file paths
docs.ZIP_EXTRACT: extract everything, returns the number of files
docs.ZIP_WRITE: archive from names and texts, without a detour through files
